analyst_view.overall: Lyon are in a coaching change: Paulo Fonseca has left for Sporting CP and assistant Jorge Maciel is in interim charge for his second game, three days after a draw at Real Sociedad in the Europa League. Ernest Nuamah and Moussa Niakhate return after missing that trip, but Lyon are still without Openda, Sulc, Morton, Ouedraogo and Himbert. Brest, under Julien Lachuer, beat Lorient 2-0 on Monday but are without centre-backs Brendan Chardonnet and Raphael Le Guen, with Lucas Tousart expected to partner Gautier Lloris at the back.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Brest's makeshift centre-back pairing and Nuamah's return argue for more goals, while Lyon's tired legs, the coaching upheaval and the absence of Openda and Sulc argue for fewer. Those roughly cancel out, so we stay close to the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, split almost evenly. Brest have Ludovic Ajorque as a target up front and Lyon will be without several attackers, but nothing in the news moves us clearly away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Jeremy Stinat is the referee, and neither side has suspension or discipline issues in the news, so we have no reason to move.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.0 shots. Lyon are three days on from a trip to San Sebastian and in their second game under an interim coach, so they may manage the tempo rather than press. Nuamah's return helps, but without Openda and Sulc we still lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Brest have been scoring well (10 goals in their last six) and Lyon's back line has Niakhate back, while Lyon's attack is weakened but gets Nuamah back. Nothing points clearly either way.
